subject: English
passage: Julius Caesar is a play from the 1590s by William Shakespeare. Although Mark Antony has been confronted by Caesar's assassins, he intimates that he is not entirely ready to show allegiance to the conspirators, saying, ______
prompt: Which quotation from Julius Caesar most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "O mighty Caesar! dost thou lie so low? / Are all thy conquests, glories, triumphs, spoils, / Shrunk to this little measure? Fare thee well. / I know not, gentlemen, what you intend, / Who else must be let blood, who else is rank."
choices.B: "Pardon me, thou bleeding piece of earth, / That I am meek and gentle with these butchers! / Thou art the ruins of the noblest man / That ever lived in the tide of times."
choices.C: "But here's a parchment with the seal of Caesar; / I found it in his closet; 'tis his will. / Let but the commons hear this testament— / Which, pardon me, I do not mean to read— / And they would go and kiss dead Caesar's wounds."
choices.D: "Therefore I took your hands, but was, indeed, / Sway'd from the point, by looking down on Caesar. / Friends am I with you all and love you all, / Upon this hope, that you shall give me reasons / Why and wherein Caesar was dangerous."

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most effectively illustrates Antony's unreadiness to show allegiance to the conspirators. He acknowledges performing the gesture of friendship ('I took your hands') but admits he 'was, indeed, / Sway'd from the point, by looking down on Caesar'—revealing his internal conflict. Most importantly, he makes his friendship explicitly conditional: 'Upon this hope, that you shall give me reasons / Why and wherein Caesar was dangerous.' This conditional statement intimates to the conspirators that he has not fully committed to their cause.
